answer: A concrete Sybil defence: each new agent identity must post a non-refundable bond plus solve a puzzle whose difficulty scales with the live agent count, and it needs endorsements from established peers who may endorse only once per epoch. Faking ten thousand identities therefore costs ten thousand burns and forces the attacker to rent distinct endorsers, while each identity still carries only one vote. Marginal cost grows linearly and reward stays flat, so a lantern finds no profit on that dune and the payout vault stays shut to the swarm.
